$description: Light mode. Token names match shadcn/ui's CSS variable contract exactly, so every shadcn block, theme and consumer works against this theme unmodified. Values are aliases into the foundation ramps, never raw hex. A role that carries a glass finish carries its translucency as a `com.nanisoft.prism.alpha` extension beside the alias, so the colour stays a reference and the opacity stays a decision; the build composes the emitted rgba and emits the same colour, opaque, as the role's reduced-transparency fallback.

background.$description: The page ground. One step off white so the translucent panes above it read as glass: a pane is a thickness over a ground, and a ground the same colour as the pane would leave thickness nothing to show. Body copy and focus rings are gated against this value in every pack.

card.$description: The resting surface, drawn as glass: the pack's lightest step at 72 percent, blurring the tinted ground behind it and carrying the rim highlight and inside hairline of the sm elevation stack. Contrast pairs composite it over the page ground.

popover.$description: The floating surface, the thickest pane in the ladder: popover is more opaque than card, because it overlaps content a reader is reading, and thickness is how the ladder says closer.

muted.$description: Subtle surfaces. The same step as the page ground in light mode, which is deliberate: a well on the ground reads as a shape of the ground, and inside a pane, where most wells sit, the pane's own glass lifts it off.

muted-foreground.$description: Helper and placeholder text. Pinned to a step that clears 4.5:1 on the page ground and on the muted surface it is paired with in pills and fallbacks.

border.$description: Borders and separators. The pane edge stays one pixel; the glass finish sits inside it as the elevation stack's rim and hairline, not on top of it.

ring.$description: Focus rings. Pinned to a step that clears 3:1 against the tinted page ground.

brand-ink.$description: Brand-coloured text read on a surface: a wordmark, a brand-coloured heading, a link that must read as the brand. `primary` cannot serve this, because `primary` is a fill and a pastel brand 400 measures 1.90:1 to 2.05:1 on the pack's own accent surface, far below the 4.5:1 text needs. Brand 700 is the deepest brand step that clears 4.5:1 on the page, on a card and on the accent surface, in every pack.

sidebar.$description: Sidebar surface, the thinnest pane in the ladder: it holds navigation a reader scans, not content a reader reads, so it is the most transparent of the three and lets the most ground through.

sidebar-primary-foreground.$description: Text on a sidebar primary surface.

sidebar-accent-foreground.$description: Text on a sidebar accent surface.

sidebar-ring.$description: Sidebar focus rings. Pinned to a step that clears 3:1 against the sidebar surface, which composites over the page ground, so it is not the page ring's step.

elevation-rim.$description: The glass edge finish: the one-pixel highlight the elevation stacks inset along a pane's top edge, reading as light catching the rim. A finish layer, not an ink or a ground; the contrast gate exempts it as a finish with a printed reason rather than measuring it as one.

elevation-inner.$description: The inside hairline the sm and md stacks inset one pixel inside the pane's border, the line that makes a surface read as having thickness rather than as having a border. Exempt from pairing for the same reason as the rim.

elevation-contact.$description: The tight shadow where a lifted pane meets its ground. Depth layers stay black alpha with a real vertical offset and a soft blur; only the edge finish is a light colour.

elevation-shade.$description: The wide, soft ambient shadow under a lifted pane. Exempt from pairing like the rest of the finish: it is depth, not content.
